thread:
alice_support: FYI — incoming ticket from @AcmeOps, multiple 429s on POST /v1/generate starting ~2024-11-10T10:12Z. They included a sample request-id and headers. Can we triage quickly?

lucas_cs: customer says the burst is from ~120 workers (pooled microservices) all doing short sync requests, each ~10 req/min. They see Retry-After: 30 and X-RateLimit-RPM: 1200 in responses.

tom_sre: Can you paste the edge log lines for one of the req ids? I'll grep and check upstream rates.

alice_support: Pasted minimal log snippet for req=req_0a1b2c3d:
```
edge-proxy [2024-11-10T10:12:02Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d status=429 route=/v1/generate tenant=acmeops rpm=1250 tpm=18000 Retry-After=30
edge-proxy [2024-11-10T10:12:02Z] backend=server-12 latency_ms=48
```

maya_eng: Quick read: tenant RPM ~1250 > tenant_rpm_limit (1000). TPM also close to configured tenant_tpm_limit. No evidence of backend failures — 429s are explicit rate-limits from the edge. Are they on any temporary burst allowance?

lucas_cs: They are on Startup plan, no burst override or reserved capacity.

maya_eng: Root cause looks like client-side concurrency + sync retries aligning with our minute window. When many clients hit the same minute boundary we see short spikes over the RPM quota. Repro: spawn 120 workers with fixed schedule -> minute-aligned peak.

tom_sre: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Temporary quota bump for acmeops to 1500 RPM for 1 hour (ops path). 2) Edge smoothing: enable token-bucket smoothing (spread tokens across the minute). 3) Ask customer to add jitter and cap concurrency.

alice_support: Sent actionable reply to customer: implement random jitter (uniform 0-5s), exponential backoff on 429 with cap, and reduce concurrency from 120 -> 60. Also offered 1-hr quota bump while they roll out fixes.

customer_user: Thanks, we applied a concurrency cap and jitter within 10m. After that the 429 rate dropped to zero. We'll need a follow-up postmortem and recommended config to avoid this.

maya_eng: For postmortem we'll grab: per-minute tenant histograms, request concurrency distribution, KV cache hit ratio, and client request patterns. Suggest adding an alert: tenant > 85% of rpm_limit for 3 consecutive minutes. Also document best-practice client-side throttles (cap concurrency, jitter, honor Retry-After).

tom_sre: I'll apply the temporary quota bump now and create the alert. Assigning follow-up to @maya_eng.

alice_support: Noted in the ticket, sent docs link: https://docs.redwood.ai/rate-limits#smoothing and included sample backoff snippet.

lucas_cs: :thumbsup: Customer confirmed 429s cleared after their client changes and the temp bump.

customer_user: Appreciate the quick help — please include example client code in the postmortem (we're using node).

maya_eng: Will attach node snippet and the repro harness. Also adding recommendation to auto-jitter scheduled jobs to avoid minute alignment.

alice_support: Closing the immediate thread, moving to ticket for postmortem owners.
